title: Three Months and One Short Chair
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：polish　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 polish 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the father ① applyed the polish that no neighbour in the house would have recorded, and he said the applying was the whole of the month. The ② polish, meaning the shine itself and not the chair, ran three months and stayed unrecorded in the book; polish, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ sort of polish in that house had the same short chair beside it, and the ④ polish at the far door, meaning the box they kept for the children to carry and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Polish, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the father said the recording is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the polish was the whole of the matter, meaning the care and not the shine. The ⑥ polish, meaning the care and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; polish, he said, is either something you apply or the only word that means both shine and a care. He said the care is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ polish had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short chair. The ⑧ polish of the whole thing, the father wrote in September, was one house and three months of recording; polish, he said, is either the box at the far door or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ polish I remember is the polish recorded in the letter, which closed in 1968 and is still recorded as the quietest in the house. ⑩ Polish, my mother said in 1970, is the only thing that improves by being recorded; all polish, she said, is a care that has agreed to look like shine. She said the care was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 擦光剂；上光（指老屋里每一样旁边的那一样）
B. n. 擦光剂；上光（指那层擦光剂本身，与小小的板凳相对）
C. 固定搭配：apply the polish 擦上这一层擦光剂
D. n. 擦光剂；上光（指留给孩子们搬的那一只）
E. n. 擦光剂之事（抽象总称，指一处老屋的擦光剂之事）
F. n. 擦光剂；上光（指家书里写到、被记载的那一层）
G. n. 擦光剂、讲究（指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 讲究（抽象总称，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: applyed the polish that no neighbour in the house would have recorded
The polish, meaning the shine itself and not the chair
Every sort of polish in that house
the polish at the far door
the polish was the whole of the matter
the polish had become a line in a letter
The polish of the whole thing

answers.why: apply the polish 意为“擦上这一层擦光剂”，1961 年那位父亲把老屋里没有一位邻居肯记载的一层擦光剂做了一遍。
polish 意为“擦光剂；上光”，指那层擦光剂本身而不是小小的板凳，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被记载。
polish 意为“擦光剂；上光”，指老屋里每一样旁边的那一样，每一样旁边都有同一张小小的板凳。
polish 意为“擦光剂；上光”，指最远那道门口的留给孩子们搬的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
polish 意为“擦光剂、讲究”，指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这层讲究就是那件事的全部。
polish 意为“讲究”，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西而不是那层擦光剂，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
polish 意为“擦光剂；上光”，指家书里写到、被记载的那一层，到 1966 年这一层成了家书里的一行。
polish 意为“擦光剂之事”，父亲九月写道，整件事的擦光剂之事是一处老屋和三个月份的记载。
polish 意为“擦光剂；上光”，我记得的是家书里记载过的那一层，1968 年搬完了，至今仍被说成老屋里最安静的一层。
polish 为抽象总称，母亲 1970 年说，擦光剂是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的擦光剂。
